import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 36

*References:*
* [Gr24] [Green's Open Problems #36](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.36)
* [CKS05] Cohn, H., Kleinberg, R., Szegedy, B., and Umans, C. "Group-theoretic Algorithms for
  Matrix Multiplication" (Problem 4.7)
-/

open Filter
open scoped Pointwise

namespace Green36

/-- The simultaneous double product property [CKS05, 4.1]. -/
def SimultaneousDoubleProduct {ι H : Type*} [AddCommGroup H]
    (A B : ι → Finset H) : Prop :=
  open scoped Classical in
  (∀ i, (A i + B i).card = (A i).card * (B i).card) ∧
  (∀ i j k, i ≠ k → Disjoint (A i + B j) (A j + B k))

/-- A variant of the simultaneous double product property, as stated in [Gr24, Problem 36]. -/
def Green36Property {ι H : Type*} [AddCommGroup H]
    (A B : ι → Finset H) : Prop :=
  open scoped Classical in
  (∀ i, (A i + B i).card = (A i).card * (B i).card) ∧
  (∀ i j k, j ≠ k → Disjoint (A i + B i) (A j + B k))

/--
Do the following exist, for arbitrarily large $n$? An abelian group $H$ with $|H| = n^{2+o(1)}$,
together with subsets $A_1, ..., A_n, B_1, ..., B_n$ satisfying $|A_i||B_i| \ge n^{2-o(1)}$ and
$|A_i + B_i| = |A_i||B_i|$, such that the sets $A_i + B_i$ are disjoint from the sets $A_j + B_k$
($j \neq k$)?

NOTE: according to [CKS05, 4.1], the conditions should be $A_i + B_j$ disjoint from $A_j + B_k$ for
$i \neq k$. See `green_36.variants.cks05`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20]
theorem green_36 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
        ∃ (H : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup H) (_ : Finite H) (A B : Fin n → Finset H),
          (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) ≤ Nat.card H ∧ Nat.card H ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (2 + ε) ∧
          (∀ i, (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) ≤ (A i).card * (B i).card) ∧
          Green36Property A B := by
  sorry

/-- Variant using the exact simultaneous double product property from [CKS05, 4.1]. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20]
theorem green_36.variants.cks05 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
        ∃ (H : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup H) (_ : Finite H) (A B : Fin n → Finset H),
          (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) ≤ Nat.card H ∧ Nat.card H ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (2 + ε) ∧
          (∀ i, (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) ≤ (A i).card * (B i).card) ∧
          SimultaneousDoubleProduct A B := by
  sorry

-- TODO(jeangud) Add variants mentioned in [Gr24, Problem 36] comments.

end Green36

reformulations.difference: CKS Definition 4.1 uses equations involving right quotients; Lean uses maximal sumset cardinality and disjointness of sumsets, specialized to abelian groups.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For finite subsets of an abelian group, |A+B|=|A||B| means addition on A×B is injective. This is equivalent to a−a′+b−b′=0 implying a−a′=b−b′=0, the double product property. Likewise, a_i−a′_j+b_j−b′_k=0 is equivalent to a_i+b_j=a′_j+b′_k. Requiring this to imply i=k is exactly the stated disjointness when i≠k. The equivalence with the source's elementwise conditions was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

reformulations.difference: The source's little-o bounds for arbitrarily large n are expressed using ∀ ε>0 and frequently atTop, with two-sided power bounds on |H| and a uniform lower bound for every pair.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given the Lean condition, choose strictly increasing n_k using ε=1/(k+1). These witnesses have exponent errors tending to zero, uniformly over the indexed pairs, as required by the source. Conversely, any such asymptotic family supplies arbitrarily large witnesses for every fixed ε>0. Restricting to n≥2 is harmless under frequently atTop. The lower bound on |H| is also implied by the pair-size bound and |A_i||B_i|=|A_i+B_i|≤|H| for positive n; this implication was checked in Lean. The same asymptotic argument applies to the CKS variant.

reformulations.difference: The variant uses CKS's disjointness of A_i+B_j and A_j+B_k for i≠k, rather than Green's diagonal-versus-off-diagonal disjointness.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Replacing every A_i by −A_i converts the conditions: SimultaneousDoubleProduct A B ↔ Green36Property (fun i => −A i) B. Negation preserves each cardinality and preserves injectivity of the pairwise sum map. It is an involution, so the conversion works both ways while leaving H, n and every quantitative bound unchanged. Although the raw predicates can differ on the same families, the complete existence claims are equivalent. This full right-hand-side equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean, without using either sorry theorem.
